agency_full: Roscosmos / Soviet Academy of Sciences (lead, IKI) — international payload from ESA / CNES / Hungary / Austria / Bulgaria / Czechoslovakia / Poland / East Germany
payload: 4920 kg flyby bus + ~1500 kg descent module (Venera-type lander + first-of-kind helium balloon aerostat). Twin spacecraft Vega 1 / Vega 2 launched 6 days apart for the same Venus-then-Halley itinerary.
credit: © Roscosmos / IKI / international consortium. Vega 1 lifted off from Baikonur 1984-12-15 carrying a Soviet Venus lander descended from the Venera line plus an ESA / CNES-built helium aerostat (balloon) — the first balloon deployment in another planet's atmosphere. The descent module separated 1985-06-09 and entered Venus's atmosphere 1985-06-11. The balloon drifted at ~54 km altitude for 46.5 hours, transmitting wind + temperature data via a 20-station global radio network. The bus, freed of its descent mass, used Venus gravity assist to redirect to comet 1P/Halley, achieving closest approach (8890 km) on 1986-03-06 — three days ahead of Vega 2, and a week ahead of ESA's Giotto, which used Vega's flyby position fix to navigate its own 596 km Halley flyby. This made Vega 1 the first-ever spacecraft to carry science instruments to two distinct solar-system targets in a single mission.
